content: {"findings":[{"file":"index.js","line":205,"severity":"critical","message":"The new regex for stripping 'www.' introduces a false positive: it matches 'www.www.example.com' (which should NOT have www stripped, as 'www' is a subdomain under 'www.example.com'). The old regex had a negative lookahead `(?!www\\.)` to prevent this. The new regex lacks this protection and would incorrectly strip 'www.' from 'www.www.example.com', changing the hostname to 'www.example.com'."},{"file":"index.js","line":205,"severity":"major","message":"The new regex introduces false negatives for valid hostnames: (1) Requires domain label (part between www. and TLD) to be 2-63 chars, but RFC allows 1-63 chars. Hostnames like 'www.a.com' will no longer have www stripped. (2) Limits TLD to 2-5 chars of only [a-z.], but valid TLDs can be up to 63 chars and include hyphens/digits (e.g., '.museum' 6 chars, '.travel' 6 chars, '.photography' 11 chars, IDN TLDs like '.xn--mgbaam7a8h'). (3) TLD pattern `[a-z.]{2,5}` allows dots but max 5 chars total, so 'co.uk' (5) works but 'com.au' (6) fails."}]}
